sources.title: Apache CouchDB Insecure Default Initialization of Resource Vulnerability
sources.snippet: Apache CouchDB: Apache CouchDB contains an insecure default initialization of resource vulnerability which can allow an attacker to escalate to administrative privileges. Required action: Apply updates per vendor instructions.
supports: CISA KEV identifies CVE-2022-24706 as exploited in the wild.

sources.title: CVE-2017-12635: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: Due to differences in the Erlang-based JSON parser and JavaScript-based JSON parser, it is possible in Apache CouchDB before 1.7.0 and 2.x before 2.1.1 to submit _users documents with duplicate keys for 'roles' used for access control within the database, including the special case '_admin' role, that denotes administrative users. In combination with CVE-2017-12636 (Remote Code Execution), this can be used to give non-admin users access to arbitrary shell commands on the server as the database system user. The JSON parser differences result in behaviour that if two 'roles' keys are available in the JSON, the second one will be used for authorising the document write, but the first 'roles' key is used for subsequent authorization for the newly created user. By design, users can not assign themselves roles. The vulnerability allows non-admin users to give themselves admin privileges.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2017-12635 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2018-11769: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: CouchDB administrative users before 2.2.0 can configure the database server via HTTP(S). Due to insufficient validation of administrator-supplied configuration settings via the HTTP API, it is possible for a CouchDB administrator user to escalate their privileges to that of the operating system's user under which CouchDB runs, by bypassing the blacklist of configuration settings that are not allowed to be modified via the HTTP API. This privilege escalation effectively allows a CouchDB admin user to gain arbitrary remote code execution, bypassing CVE-2017-12636 and CVE-2018-8007.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2018-11769 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2018-8007: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: Apache CouchDB administrative users can configure the database server via HTTP(S). Due to insufficient validation of administrator-supplied configuration settings via the HTTP API, it is possible for a CouchDB administrator user to escalate their privileges to that of the operating system's user that CouchDB runs under, by bypassing the blacklist of configuration settings that are not allowed to be modified via the HTTP API. This privilege escalation effectively allows an existing CouchDB admin user to gain arbitrary remote code execution, bypassing already disclosed CVE-2017-12636. Mitigation: All users should upgrade to CouchDB releases 1.7.2 or 2.1.2.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2018-8007 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2010-0009: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: Apache CouchDB 0.8.0 through 0.10.1 allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information by measuring the completion time of operations that verify (1) hashes or (2) passwords.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2010-0009 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2010-2234: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Apache CouchDB 0.8.0 through 0.11.0 allows remote attackers to hijack the authentication of administrators for direct requests to an installation URL.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2010-2234 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.
